subject: BrightShore renewal — concession request (credit + SLA)
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@brightshore.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: renewals@brightshore.com
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal quote — performance impact & request for credit/SLA

Hi Ben,

We're reviewing the renewal quote you sent for BrightShore's enterprise license (250 seats). Before we proceed, Procurement flagged the service interruptions in Jan/Feb that impacted two regional clusters — SLA was missed twice and we had to fall back to cached results for a day. We've attached our internal incident summary.

Given the customer impact, procurement is asking for: 1) a one-time service credit to offset the incident impact (their ask: 25% of ARR for the year), and 2) a contractual SLA guarantee (99.9% monthly) for the next 12 months or a credit mechanism tied to uptime.

They're otherwise willing to renew but will consider alternative vendors if we can't address these items. Can you review and confirm what concessions are possible? We need a counter-proposal by Tuesday EOD.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Head of AI Integrations
BrightShore

Attachment: support-incident-log.pdf (summary, 9 pages)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal quote — performance impact & request for credit/SLA

Folks — escalating BrightShore renewal. Customer is high ACV (~$180k ARR) and strategic (vertical reference). They asked for a 25% one-time credit and a 12-month 99.9% SLA guarantee tied to credits.

Quick notes:
- Current renewal quote (attached) is $720k for 3 years; requested credit equates to ~$180k one-time, which is > deal desk threshold.
- We had two incidents in Jan/Feb; incident log attached shows root-cause and mitigation steps. Customer is upset but willing to renew if we show meaningful remediation.

My recommended path (preserve revenue and limit precedent):
1) Offer a one-time credit of $45,000 (roughly 6% of first-year ARR) instead of 25% ask.
2) Add a 6-month SLA pilot/addendum with specific metrics and an agreed credit table for breach limited to the pilot period.
3) Reset the annual renewal date to align with support improvements (term reset of 6 months) — effectively delaying next renewal by six months.

This combination reduces immediate cash hit while giving the customer contractual comfort. Approvals required: any credit > $25k needs VP/exec sign-off and Finance sign-off on the concession memo. Legal will need to confirm SLA wording.

Can we get an exec decision by EOD Tuesday (3/17)? I will also prepare the concession-approval-form for Finance.

Attachments: renewal-quote-BS-2026v2.pdf; support-incident-log.pdf; concession-approval-form.xlsx

— Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal quote — performance impact & request for credit/SLA

Ben — thanks for the summary. A few customer-success observations:
- BrightShore has been scaling usage quickly; churn risk is real if they feel discounted.
- We've already committed to a couple of engineering mitigations (regional failover tuning) that will be in place in ~3 weeks.

From CS perspective my preferred offer:
- $35k one-time credit (to show meaningful remediation)
- 6-month term reset (so they see improvements before the 'renewal' pressure)
- SLA addendum limited to a pilot: 6 months with a capped credit schedule (no more than $15k in total credits during pilot)

This is a compromise between Ben's conservative ask and the customer's demand. Concern: setting a precedent on credit % — recommend we document as a one-off concession with an approval memo.

Happy to join the call with Olivia if we need to negotiate live.

— Marissa
Director, Customer Success
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal quote — performance impact & request for credit/SLA

I've reviewed the SLA language and the concession form. Legal is OK with a short pilot SLA provided we: 1) limit aggregate financial exposure during the pilot, 2) include a clause that this pilot does not create a recurring SLA commitment beyond the agreed term, and 3) require BrightShore to sign an amendment accepting the pilot scope.

My suggested formal offer: $30,000 one-time credit + 6-month term reset + 6-month SLA pilot with a capped credit schedule (max $15k during pilot). I also updated the concession-approval-form with the legal notes and DocuSign envelope (link below). Finance will want a signed memo.

DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/envelope/EE-9A3B2C

If you want to reduce customer friction, we can split the difference to $35k credit, but need Exec sign-off for >$25k.

— Rishi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal quote — performance impact & request for credit/SLA

Appreciate the analysis and options. I'm approving a one-time credit of $35,000, the 6-month term reset, and a 6-month SLA pilot with the capped credit schedule (legal's cap of $15k during pilot). Conditions:
- We document this as a one-off concession (concession-approval-form.xlsx) and obtain Finance sign-off before sending the amendment.
- Legal to finalize the SLA addendum wording and ensure the pilot clause includes non-precedent language.
- Ben: send the revised quote and DocuSign amendment to Olivia; cc Marissa for implementation and Rishi for legal sign-off.

Ben — proceed with the $35k offer and push the DocuSign by Monday. If BrightShore insists on more, escalate back to me with churn forecast.

— Vivek
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
